To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
epithelial cells from mouse vas deference can express the tissue specific protein MVDP in response to androgenic stimulation only in culture conditions that allow cell polarization.

epithelial cells isolated and subcultured from mouse vas deferers express MVDP in vitro in response to androgen treatment, but that they require a minimal serum-free medium supplemented with hormones and growth factors.

epithelial cells from mouse vas deference can be subcultured in vitro and that the expression of a tissue specific protein, MVDP, in these cells in response to testosterone is dependent on the polarization of the cells and on the presence of a specific serum free medium.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a model system to study in vitro the mechanisms of androgen action on a target cell, and to study in vivo the role of MVDP in the physiology of the male reproductive tract.
the development of a serum-free defined culture system for the study of androgen action on epithelial cells of the male reproductive tract.

the establishment of epithelial cell cultures from mouse vas deference which can be amplified and which respond to androgens in a dose-dependent way, allowing the study of the molecular mechanisms of androgen action on the vas deferens.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the epithelial cell subculture is an excellent in vitro model for the study of the regulation of androgenic induction in epithelial cells of mouse vas deferens.

the expression of MVVP in epithelial cells from vas deferens is a specific androgen dependent response which requires a highly defined culture system and that it is a reliable and reproducible model for the study of androgen action in epithelial cells.
the androgenic induction is dependent upon the epithelial cells being in a polarized state, and that this is a requirement for expression of the androgen-dependent MVDP.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the epithelial cell culture from mouse vas deference is a useful model for the study of epithelial cell differentiation and androgen action.
the epithelial cells of the vas deferens are able to differentiate in vitro and express a specific protein in response to androgenic hormones.
epithelial cell cultures obtained from mouse vas deferents are a good model system for studying androgen action in the male reproductive tract.
The main takeaway from our work is that
epithelial cells from the male reproductive tract can be maintained in culture in an undifferentiated state.
the expression of MVDB is a very specific response to androgen and that it requires the polarization of epithelial cells in culture.
the androgenic induction system of MVDP expression in mouse epithelial cell cultures provides a model for studying the molecular mechanisms of androgenic regulation in a well-defined cellular system.
